report.summary: checkoutservice pod is healthy by Kubernetes metrics (Running, Ready, 0 restarts) and has 0% error rate, but the 5m CPU limit causes the container to be throttled 53% of the time, producing the observed latency climb. This is local resource saturation caused by aggressive CPU quota.
report.root_cause: CPU resource limit of 5m (5 millicores) in the checkoutservice pod specification is too low for the synchronous request-handling workload, causing the container to be CPU-throttled 0.53 seconds per second, directly producing the reported latency climb.
evidence: Pod spec shows cpu_limit: 5m on server container (get_workload_status: containers[0].cpu_limit='5m')
Container CPU throttling rate: 0.5326 seconds per second (query_prometheus: rate(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total{pod='checkoutservice-5646d8d9fd-z2srb'}[5m])=0.5326)
Error rate is 0: grpc_server_handled_total with grpc_code!=OK returns empty result (query_prometheus: no errors, 100% success rate)
Pod is Running and Ready with 0 restarts (get_workload_status: phase='Running', ready=true, restart_count=0)
Revision 15 deployed 2026-08-19T06:50:33Z (get_rollout_history: revision 15 created at 2026-08-19T06:50:33Z), timing aligns with reported latency degradation onset
Symptom profile (latency climbing + 100% success rate) is textbook CPU throttling behavior, not application error or dependency failure
alternatives: Downstream dependency degradation (score 0.15): rejected because error rate is exactly 0 (all requests succeed), container-level CPU throttling measured locally rules out I/O wait, and dependency failures produce errors not pure latency with success

Node-level resource saturation (score 0.12): rejected because CPU throttling is enforced at the container level—the 5m limit itself causes throttling regardless of node free capacity, and no competing heavy workloads are visible on node k3d-sre-lab-agent-1
report.impact: Checkout requests experience increased latency, degrading user experience and likely checkout conversion rates. All requests still succeed (0% error rate), but response time SLA is violated. Incident is contained to checkoutservice performance only; no cascade to dependent services.

remediation.action: Increase CPU limit for checkoutservice container from 5m to 200m (or higher based on observed baseline traffic patterns).
remediation.command: kubectl set resources deployment checkoutservice -c=server --limits=cpu=200m -n boutique
remediation.rationale: The 5m limit is being hit constantly (53% throttle rate). Increasing to 200m will allow the container to execute requests without sustained throttling. Once applied, monitor latency metrics (e.g., histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(grpc_server_handling_seconds_bucket))) to confirm recovery. If still slow, increase further (e.g., 500m) based on baseline traffic patterns.

against: CPU throttling is measured at the container level—the pod's own 5m limit is actively enforcing throttling regardless of node load
No competing heavy workloads visible on that node in get_workload_status output
Even with abundant free node resources, a 5m CPU limit on a synchronous request handler would still throttle and cause latency; node-level contention would only make it worse, not explain it
